title: Asynchronous Lifetime and Coroutine Data Race
platform_conditions: C++11 threads and C++20 coroutines on any conforming toolchain; manifestation depends on scheduler timing and memory model
security_mechanism: A detached std::thread constructed with `[this]() {...}` captures the raw pointer; when the owning object is destroyed (request ends, parent returns) the still-running thread dereferences freed memory, and there is no join or signal to stop it. The intended fix — enable_shared_from_this — only works when the object is already owned by a shared_ptr and shared_from_this() is called after construction; calling it in a constructor or on a stack object throws or produces an empty weak reference, so a superficially 'fixed' version can still dangle. C++20 coroutines repeat the pattern at co_await boundaries: frame suspension may outlive the caller's scope, so parameters passed by reference and locals referenced across co_await dangle when the coroutine resumes after its parent returned. Non-atomic shared state mutated from the callback is simultaneously a data race (undefined behavior under the C++ memory model).

source_sink_clues.source: Request lifetime boundaries: completion callbacks, detached workers, timers, and coroutine resumptions that execute after the request context or session object was destroyed.
source_sink_clues.sink: std::thread(...).detach() or stored callback capturing `this`; shared_from_this()/weak_ptr misuse; coroutine lambdas taking reference parameters and referencing locals across co_await

tracking_guards: Check that asynchronous work owns the object through shared_ptr taken via enable_shared_from_this BEFORE launching (and that the object is managed by shared_ptr at all), that detached threads are replaced by scoped joinable threads (std::jthread) or an explicit stop mechanism, and that coroutine parameters are taken by value and no local is referenced across a co_await.
not_candidate_when: The thread/callback is joined or awaited before the owner can be destroyed, ownership is carried by a shared_ptr captured by value and the object's lifetime is provably covered, or the coroutine is consumed to completion within the parent scope (no suspension escapes).
public_references: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html
C++ Core Guidelines: CP concurrency rules — https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines
